notes: Free. Opening hours change with the season.

name: Bibliothèque nationale de France
what: Free Salle Ovale reading room, open to everyone.
notes: Salle Ovale is free, all ages, no booking. Tue 10:00–20:00; Wed–Sun 10:00–18:00. Closed Monday, public holidays, Easter Sunday, and Pentecost Sunday. Open on 8 May, Ascension Thursday, 1 Nov, and 11 Nov. BnF museum exhibitions are ticketed.
hours: Tue 10:00–20:00. Wed–Sun 10:00–18:00. Closed Monday, public holidays, Easter Sunday, and Pentecost Sunday

name: Le Bon Marché
what: Department store to wander; free to enter.
notes: Free to browse. Mon–Wed and Fri–Sat 10:00–20:00, Thu 10:00–20:45, Sun 11:00–20:00.

name: La Bourse et La Vie
what: French bistro. Peppery steak au poivre with house-cut frites and house salad.
notes: Beli 9.7 (€€€). One of their favorite bistros; a first stop every time they are in Paris. Closed Sat–Sun; open Mon–Fri for lunch and dinner. Lunch plats du jour from €24; dinner mains from €36; desserts from €10.

name: Chez l'Ami Louis
what: Classic bistro. Côte de boeuf.
notes: Beli 9.1 (€€€€). Called both the world's most famous bistro and the worst restaurant in Paris.
hours: Wed–Sat 12:00–14:30 and 19:30–23:30. Sun 12:30–14:30 and 19:30–23:30. Closed Monday and Tuesday.

name: La Renommée
what: French restaurant. Filet au poivre.
notes: Beli 10.0 (€€€). Their no. 1 ranked Paris restaurant; beef they call the best they have found in Paris. Sister of New York’s 4 Charles. Sun–Thu dinner 17:30–22:30; Fri–Sat lunch 12:00–14:00 and dinner 17:30–22:30. Dinner reservations open 30 days ahead at 09:00; parties of 1–8; card required; €50 per person if cancelled within 24 hours.
hours: Sun–Thu dinner 17:30–22:30. Fri–Sat lunch 12:00–14:00 and dinner 17:30–22:30

name: Bistrot Paul Bert
what: Bistro. Steak in creamy pepper sauce.
notes: Beli card 9.7 (€€€); voiceover says 9.8. Most famous spot on their list; pepper sauce they call the best they have ever had. Beloved by locals and tourists. Closed Sun–Mon; Tue–Sat 12:00–14:00 and 19:30–23:00.

name: Palais Garnier
what: Self-guided visit of the opera house interior
notes: Best €15 you'll ever spend; air conditioning inside. Online booking mandatory; no visit tickets sold on site. Last admission one hour before closing. Auditorium often closed for rehearsals.

name: Rue des Francs-Bourgeois
what: The Marais shopping street. Independent clothes, concept shops, and the Place des Vosges end.
notes: Walk the stretch between Place des Vosges and the Rue des Archives.

name: Rue Saint-Honoré
what: The long shopping street through the 1st. Designer windows around Place Vendôme.
notes: The useful stretch is between Palais Royal and the Madeleine, not the whole street.

name: Avenue Montaigne
what: The couture avenue. Dior, Chanel, and the other big houses.
notes: A short walk south of the Champs-Élysées. Windows more than baskets.

name: Rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré
what: The other couture street, west of the Madeleine. Hermès and the palace side.
notes: Continues the Saint-Honoré shops past Rue Royale.

name: Passage Jouffroy
what: 1840s covered passage. Bookshops, toys, and the Musée Grévin entrance.
notes: Across the boulevard from Passage des Panoramas. Free to walk through.

name: Passage Verdeau
what: The third covered passage in the row, quieter than Jouffroy. Old cameras, prints, and small shops.
notes: Continue north from Passage Jouffroy. Free to walk through.

name: Rue des Martyrs
what: The sloping food-and-shop street from Notre-Dame-de-Lorette up toward Pigalle.
notes: Bakeries and small shops the whole way up. Busier on Sunday morning.

name: Rue Bonaparte
what: Saint-Germain shopping street. Galleries, clothes, and the church at the top.
notes: The useful bit is between the Seine and Boulevard Saint-Germain.

name: Galeries Lafayette
what: The big department store. Free 8th-floor terrace, with Garnier and the Eiffel Tower in the view.
notes: Free to walk in. The roof is the reason to go up. Next door to Printemps.

name: Printemps
what: The other Haussmann department store. Art nouveau cupola, and the 7ème Ciel rooftop bar.
notes: Across the street from Galeries Lafayette. Free to walk in. The roof bar is 7ème Ciel.

name: La Samaritaine
what: Reopened department store on the Seine. The glass roof and the view from the top.
notes: Free to enter. By Pont Neuf, between the Louvre and Châtelet.

name: Le BHV Marais
what: The Marais department store, across from the Hôtel de Ville. Home floor downstairs, fashion above.
notes: Officially Bazar de l'Hôtel de Ville. Free to walk in.

name: Westfield Forum des Halles
what: The underground mall under the Les Halles canopy. Chain shops, a cinema, and the Châtelet exits.
notes: Useful if it is raining. The canopy park is above it.

name: Carnaby Street
what: The pedestrian shopping street off Regent Street. Side lanes have the smaller shops.
notes: Newburgh Street and Kingly Court are the better detours off the main strip.

name: New Bond Street
what: Mayfair's jewellery and fashion street, from Oxford Street down toward Piccadilly.
notes: Old Bond Street continues it to the south. Windows, not a browse-everything walk.

name: Regent Street
what: The curved shopping street from Oxford Circus toward Piccadilly Circus.
notes: Liberty is on the west side. The lights go up in November.

name: Jermyn Street
what: The shirt and shoe street, one block south of Piccadilly.
notes: Short. Paired with Fortnum and Mason on Piccadilly.

name: Savile Row
what: The tailoring street, parallel to Bond Street.
notes: A look at the windows is the visit. Appointments are a different trip.

name: Marylebone High Street
what: A village high street of bookshops, clothes, and food shops, north of Oxford Street.
notes: Daunt Books is the one to go in. Quieter than Regent Street.

name: King's Road
what: Chelsea's long shopping street, from Sloane Square west.
notes: The useful stretch is the SW3 part near Sloane Square, not the far western end.

name: Portobello Road
what: The market street. Antiques at the south end, clothes and food further up.
notes: Saturday is the full market. Weekdays are the shops that stay open.

name: Seven Dials
what: The seven-street junction in Covent Garden. Small shops off the sundial pillar.
notes: Neal Street and Earlham Street run off it. A short walk from Neal's Yard.

name: Burlington Arcade
what: The covered Regency arcade from Piccadilly to Burlington Gardens. Jewellers and small luxury shops.
notes: Free to walk through. Beadles still patrol it.

name: Floral Street
what: The clothes street behind the Royal Opera House, quieter than the piazza.
notes: Parallel to Long Acre. A few minutes from Covent Garden station.

name: Redchurch Street
what: The short Shoreditch shopping street. Independent clothes and a few good cafés.
notes: Between Brick Lane and Shoreditch High Street. Small; one walk covers it.

name: Liberty
what: The Tudor-front department store. Fabrics, the atrium, and the rooms upstairs.
notes: Free to walk in. The mock-Tudor building is on Great Marlborough Street, off Regent Street.

name: Selfridges
what: The Oxford Street department store. The window displays and the food hall.
notes: Free to walk in. Duke Street entrance is the quieter one.

name: Harrods
what: The Knightsbridge department store. The food halls are the part worth the crowd.
notes: Free to enter. A dress code is posted at the door.

name: Fortnum & Mason
what: The Piccadilly grocer. Hampers, the food hall, and the clock outside.
notes: Free to walk in. Across from the Royal Academy.

name: Harvey Nichols
what: The other Knightsbridge department store, smaller and more fashion than Harrods.
notes: Free to walk in. The fifth floor is the restaurant and food shop.

name: Westfield London
what: The big west London mall. Useful for chains in one building when it is raining.
notes: Shepherd's Bush stations are on the doorstep. Not a walk from the hotel.

name: Battersea Power Station
what: Shops inside the old power station, plus the chimney lift if you want the view.
notes: Free to walk the mall. The chimney is a separate ticket. Northern line to Battersea Power Station.

name: Bourse de Commerce
what: The Pinault Collection in the old commodities exchange. The rotunda, then whatever show is up.
notes: Optional. A short walk east of the Louvre.

name: Musée Zadkine
what: Ossip Zadkine's house and studio, with a sculpture garden. A small museum.
notes: Optional. South of the Luxembourg.

name: Musée des Arts et Métiers
what: Machines and instruments in an old priory. Foucault's pendulum hangs in the former church.
notes: Optional. North edge of the Marais.

name: Musée Rodin
what: The Thinker and The Kiss, in the house and in the sculpture garden.
notes: Optional. Next to Invalides. Friday 30 Oct is an open day.

name: Hôtel de Sully
what: A Marais mansion. Walk the courtyard through to Place des Vosges.
notes: On the way between Rue Saint-Antoine and the square.

name: Café de Flore
what: The Saint-Germain café. The terrace is on the boulevard.
notes: A sit-down if you are already in the 6th. Not a plan stop.

name: Les Deux Magots
what: The other Saint-Germain café, on the square by the church.
notes: Across the corner from Café de Flore.

name: Place de la Contrescarpe
what: The square at the top of Rue Mouffetard. Fountain, cafés, the start of the market street.
notes: You are already on Mouffetard on 29 Oct. This is the top of that street.
hours: Public square. Open through the day.

name: Place de la Sorbonne
what: The university square. Chapel façade, cafés, the students.
notes: Between Cluny and the Panthéon.
hours: Public square. Open through the day.

name: Cour du Commerce-Saint-André
what: A narrow covered lane of old shopfronts off Boulevard Saint-Germain.
notes: Le Procope is on this lane.

name: Clos Montmartre
what: The last working vineyard in Paris. A gate on Rue des Saules. You look in from the street.
notes: Harvest is in October. Not a walk-in museum.

name: La Maison Rose
what: The pink house at the corner of Rue de l'Abreuvoir. The picture is the façade.
notes: A few steps from the vineyard gate.

name: Moulin de la Galette
what: The windmill on Rue Lepic. Walk the street up to it.
notes: Seen from the street. The mill itself is not a visit.

name: Place Vendôme
what: The octagonal square. The column, the Ritz, the jewellers' windows.
notes: On the way between the Tuileries and Garnier.
hours: Public square. Open through the day.

name: Rue Sainte-Anne
what: The Japanese and Asian restaurant street, between Palais-Royal and the Opéra.
notes: Useful if lunch or dinner is already on this side of the Louvre.

name: Institut du Monde Arabe
what: The Arab World Institute on the quay. The terrace looks back at Notre-Dame.
notes: A short walk from the hotel. Book the terrace if you go up.

name: Jardin des Plantes
what: The botanical garden. The long alleys and the glasshouses. The zoo is a separate ticket.
notes: East of the hotel, toward the river.

name: Père Lachaise
what: The hillside cemetery. Chopin, Oscar Wilde, Jim Morrison, and a lot of walking.
notes: About 20 minutes from Badaboum, so the pin can show on 31 Oct. It is not the plan that night.

name: Parc Montsouris
what: A south-Paris park with a lake. Quiet.
notes: The 14th is not on any day's walk, so this stays off the map.

name: Cité Universitaire
what: The international student campus beside Parc Montsouris. National houses along the park.
notes: Only worth it if you are already at Montsouris.

name: Canal Saint-Martin
what: The locks and the iron footbridges. A walk along the quay.
notes: North of the Marais.
hours: The quay is open through the day.

name: Philharmonie de Paris
what: The concert hall at La Villette. The rooftop belvedere is a free walk with a view, separate from a ticket.
notes: The 19th is not on any day, so this stays off the map.

name: Bateaux-Mouches
what: A daytime Seine boat. About an hour on the river.
notes: Optional. This is not the dinner cruise, which is off the plan.

name: Bread Ahead
address: Cathedral Street, Borough Market, London SE1 9DE
what: Doughnuts at Borough Market. The crème brûlée doughnut is the one people queue for.
notes: Still at the market as of late September 2026, while a lease dispute is ongoing. Check they are still there. The market is closed Monday. 5 Nov is a Thursday.

name: Padella
what: Fresh pasta in a small Borough room. Walk-in.
notes: The pasta spot in the market.

name: The Black Pig
address: Borough Market Kitchen, Winchester Walk, London SE1
what: Sandwiches at Borough Market.
notes: A friend recommends these.

name: Notto
what: Fresh pasta, on Piccadilly.
notes: With Padella, Bancone, and Osteria Romana.

name: Bancone
what: Fresh pasta in Covent Garden.

name: Osteria Romana
what: Roman cooking in Knightsbridge.

name: Regency Cafe
what: Old-school English breakfast cafe.

name: Black Bear Burger
what: Burgers on Exmouth Market.

name: Truffle Burger
what: Burgers in Soho.

name: Shackfuyu
what: Go for the kinako french toast. A full meal is optional.
notes: Their site says the restaurant is retiring, and points the dessert at their ramen bars. Check it is still open.

name: Kova Patisserie
what: Sea salt cheese lava cake. A slice is the visit.

name: Kova Patisserie
what: Sea salt cheese lava cake. A slice is the visit.

name: Kova Patisserie
what: Sea salt cheese lava cake, on the South Kensington walk.

name: Bilmonte
what: Gelato. The one a friend insisted on. Pistachio, and the chocolate pour.

name: Layla Bakery
what: Wild-grain bakery on Portobello Road.
notes: West of the Hyde Park day, so it may sit off the map.

name: Pophams
what: Bakery.
notes: This branch is in Hackney, off the walking days.

name: Arôme
what: Honey butter toast, and the pastries.
notes: On Mercer Street in Covent Garden, a few minutes from Chinatown.

name: Hawksmoor
what: Steakhouse next to Borough Market. Known for the Sunday roast.
notes: There is no Sunday in London on this trip. It is still a steakhouse the other days.

name: Hawksmoor
what: Steakhouse near Piccadilly. Known for the Sunday roast.
notes: There is no Sunday in London on this trip.

name: Hawksmoor
what: Steakhouse in Covent Garden. Known for the Sunday roast.
notes: There is no Sunday in London on this trip.

name: Hawksmoor
what: Steakhouse in Knightsbridge. Known for the Sunday roast.
notes: There is no Sunday in London on this trip. Friday's walk is the nearby day.

name: Flat Iron
what: Steak at a set price. Good value, not the city's best steak.

name: Gymkhana
what: Mayfair Indian. Book if you go.
notes: The booked London dinner stays OMA. This is a pin for a day already in Mayfair.

name: Fallow
what: Modern British. Get the mushroom parfait. They grow the mushrooms.

name: Kiln
what: Thai grill. Super 8 group.

name: Smoking Goat
what: Thai barbecue. Super 8 group.
notes: Shoreditch is off the walking days.

name: Plaza Khao Gaeng
what: Southern Thai. Super 8 group.

name: Brat
what: Wood-fired Basque. Pricier. Super 8 group.
notes: Off the walking days.

name: Mountain
what: Wood fire, on the pricier side. Super 8 group.

name: Barrafina
what: Spanish counter in Soho.

name: Barrafina
what: Spanish counter in Covent Garden.

name: Jinli
what: Sichuan. Dry mala.
